This page holds reference to all of the main characters of the story:
Vesper Dreadway Syren Ashryver Aelyra Caladwen Elowen Giggleleaf
Played by Alex
data.backstory#Backstory:
Aelyra Caladwen is the daughter of Emporer Caladwen of the Twilight Court. As such, she grew up wealthy and well-off, but she has a rebellious streak in her that couldn’t easily be controlled. She has always had a lust for adventure, a love for music, a compassion for the less fortunate, and the drive to break free from the golden chains that had bound her. When Syren suggested to her best friend Aelyra that she wanted to leave the court in search of her sister, Aelyra jumped at the opportunity.
As she grew older and her father’s authoritarian nature became worse, and he mistreated the people, she began to speak out against him to the people, attempting to invoke a people’s rebellion. The Emporer caught on and squashed that, silencing her and locking her away until she “learned”. She would never learn, and instead decided to abscond in silence from the kingdom forever with her best friend Syren, the only other person who understands her.
data.character-traits#Character Traits: Lordly, upper-eschelon mannerisms “Do you know who I am?” Skilled musician Despite growing up wealthy and powerful, feels a connection to common and working people
data.relationships#Relationships: Close friends with Syren, grew up together in the High Court Complicated relationship with her parents, neither of whom really ever understood her indifference towards the crown

data: Played by Bri
data.backstory#Backstory: Little is known about the past of the mysterious Elowen, even to Elowen. One day, she simply awoke or appeared in the woods with no memory of her origins. She communes with the wind and wanders to wherever it takes her, looking for the next place where she can provide help. She is odd and whimsical; dreamy yet perceptive; a gentle healer and lover of nature.
data.character-traits#Character Traits: Compassionate Cares for ALL living things, no matter their nature
data.motivations#Motivations: To protect those who need protecting To be one with nature
data.relationships#Relationships: The wind seems to be a pretty tight homie tbh

data: Played by Justine
data.backstory#Backstory: Syren grew up in The Twilight Court of Squawhorn under a strict military general father. At a young age, her mother fell in love with a human (ew) and ran off from the court, leaving Syren motherless and bitter. She was fully expected to engage in military service, herself, but the discovery that she had a long-lost half-sister sparked the fire of a personal quest inside her. She must find the half-sister. When she told her lifelong friend Aelyra of her plot, her best friend agreed to accompany her, and together, they embarked on a quest east towards Estharia, the direction her mother traveled so many years before.
data.character-traits#Character Traits: She’s, like, really strong Gruff and intimidating A little bloodthirsty sometimes Protective of Aelyra Possibly a drinking problem?
data.relationships#Relationships: Close friends with Aelyra, grew up together in the High Court Complicated relationship with her parents: Father was an overbearing military man, mother left when she was young.

data.backstory#Backstory:
From Brittney:
She’s a half elf rogue who performs lute in taverns while quietly relieving wealthy patrons of their coin purses. But don’t worry, she’s not a monster. She will leave behind chocolate coins and place of stolen ones. She’s charming, a little chaotic, and extremely passionate about collecting beautiful daggers. She insists her good luck comes from a tiny, invisible duck named marzipan, which she assures everyone is completely real.
Vesper Dreadway grew up in Ratwhistle with her adoring human father Thad, from whom she adopted her affinity for knives. Her mother
data.character-traits#Character Traits: Self-Assured Standoffish and independent Of questionable morality (but “not a monster” as she says) Might be crazy with the whole duck thing, maybe?
data.marzipan#Marzipan: Marzipan is an invisible, potentially imaginary Duck to whom Vesper believes she owes her life after an incident in Ratwhistle during her childhood that nearly took her life. This duck provides much needed companionship to Vesper, who travels alone, and Vesper frequently consults her feathered friend for advice on risky situations. Is Marzipan real? Time will tell. Time… Will… Tell…
data.relationships#Relationships: A close relationship with her father Marzipan is a real one for sure

Humanoids Demons Imps Undead A few mysterious character names which have been mentioned or identified but never met:
Gwarveaux The Time Wizard

This section holds reference to all of the demon characters that have been encountered by the player characters.
Belvedere

Belvedere was Findlay’s personal servant, enslaved by a demonic contract. He was freed in Session #1 by Findlay after he had accidentally spilled tea on the demonic contracts, but then took power over the imps personally. He was killed by the player characters at the end of the session, freeing the imps and allowing them to return home to The Abyss.
Gwarveaux is the name that signed the bottom of the demonic contracts seen in Elowen’s vision at the beginning of session 2.

This section is specifically for Humanoid characters, like Humans and Elves and Dwarves.
Findlay Emporer Caladwen General Ashryver

Emporer Caladwen is the emporer Squawhorn, who sits the throne of The Twilight Court. He is the father to Aelrya Caladwen.
The Emporer is a greedy authoritarian, embezzling from or overtaxing commoners and running a fascist regime. When his daughter began publicly speaking out against him, he attempted to silence her and to force her obedience. When she disappeared, he became beset on bringing her home and molding her into the future Empress of the Twilight Court that she was born to be, whether she likes it or not.

Findlay is the owner of the Lamp Emporium in Norville. He had enslaved the demon Belvedere as his personal servent as well as several Imps as his workers, until he accidentally destroyed his demonic contracts in Session #1, freeing the demon and imps from their bonds. The players freed the imps and implored Findlay to hire paid workers in the future instead of meddling with the enslavement of demons and imps.
General Ashryver is the top general of Squawhorn, who regularly counsils with The Twilight Court and serves as its military arm. He is the father to Syren Ashryver. He is dead.

Thaddeus Miller (known as Thad) is the father of Vesper Dreadway. Described by many as a good man, Vesper would call him “the sweetest human you’ve ever met,” and a man at market in Norville called him “salt of the earth.” He gave Vesper her first dagger.
He is alive and well, still living in Ratwhistle.

This is the Elven mother of Syren and Vesper.
All we know of her is that she birthed Syren, but abandoned her early in Syren’s life, running off somewhere. She ended up in Ratwhistle, fell in love with Thad, and gave birth to Vesper. She died during childbirth.

This section holds reference to all of the imp characters that have been encountered by the player characters:
Max Biff Fog Yuck
Biff is Max’s right-hand imp. He is gruff, with a thick cockney-like accent. He fights with a club and don’t take no guff from nobody, I tells ‘ya.
Fog is one of Max’s imp followers. He is a small, grey imp with slight demonic traits. He has a New York accent and breathes plumes of smoke.

Max is the defacto leader of the imps, popular among most of them and has earned their loyalty through his own deeds. He is brown and looks quite a bit like a bat. He has been described as “very cool”. His right-hand man, best friend, and most trusted ally among the imps is Biff.
Yuck is one of the imps loyal to Belvedere. He was a slender pink cat-like imp. Vesper cut off his tail before Syren slit his throat and killed her in the first session.
The mysterious former inhabitant of the abandoned tower in session 2.

All of the details regarding Undead NPS will be here.
Skeleton

This skeleton was trapped in the study of The Abandoned Wizard’s Tower, forced to keep the study as a servant to whatever wizard once lived there. But when the tower was abandoned, the magic that worked in that place was never released, and so it worked and worked.
It was freed by the players and it said it wanted to join them, so it’ll be following along.

This is where all of the setting details will go, details that we’ve learned about the places we’ve come up with, where they are, the people and places there, etc. Organized by country.
Estharia Squawhorn
Norville is the country in which the story begins and primarily takes place. It neighbors Squawhorn.

Norville is a mid-sized trading town where travelers frequently come and go. Adventurers looking for a place to rest, merchants looking to trade, and craftspeople looking for short-term work frequently come and go.
data.findlays-lamp-emporium#Findlay\u0026rsqu:
Findlay’s Lamp Emporium is a tall, narrow, Weasley-house-esque building that is exactly what it sounds like. Findlay and his imp servants produce all manner of lamps and lamp-like objects, some of which are magical in nature. The Lamp Emporium is host to a direct portal to The Abyss, the demonic realm from whence the imps and demons came. A magical welcome mat embued with the words “Not Welcome” keeps the demons from coming into the material plane from The Abyss.
In the first session of the game, the lamp emporium is the focal point of the story. Findlay had enslaved a demon and several imps to do his bidding in the lamp shop, both personally and professionally, but he accidentally spilled tea on his demonic contracts, freeing them from their magical bindings, and they quickly overthrew Findlay and removed him from power. The player characters ultimately decided to free the imps from both Findlay’s control as well as Belvedere’s.
data.the-lute--lyre#The Lute \u0026amp; Lyre: The Lute & Lyre is a quiet tavern located in Norville. It’s run by an angel of a woman, similar to Grandma Rocky, and is frequented by day drunks and bar flies. It’s notable for having a large stage for performances, which are put to use somewhat regularly and without much schedule.

data: Ratwhistle is the hometown of Vesper Dreadway. It’s a small, quaint village, mostly inhabited by farmers who grow and tend to the farmlands, and a small band of thieves who look out for each other. They steal from other towns and bring the spoils back to Ratwhistle to share with the residents, including those who do not partake in thievery.

Squawhorn is a neighboring country to Estharia. It is a wealthy, war-waging nation and home to The Twilight Court. [Syren Ashriver](../../../main-characters/syren-ashryver and [Aelyra Caladwen](../../../main-characters/aelyra-caladwen come from this nation.
The Twilight Court
The Twilight Court is the seat of the high council of Squawhorn, the nation from which Aelyra Caladwen and Syren Ashryver hail. It is ruled by Emporer Caladwen.

data.battle-belvedere-and-huh#Battle: Belvede:
The party tenses, and Belvedere notices the tension rising in the room. He looks between the four elves and spies Elowen preparing a fiery spell. He whips around and casts his own spell on her. Her peripheral vision flashes an icy blue for a second before she hears Belvedere’s voice in her head, “kill the poisoned one”, and in that moment it becomes clear to Elowen that this is what she must do, it’s crucially important that she obey this order. With the help of Marzipan, Vesper regains her faculties just in time to see an uncharacteristically dead-eyed Elowen approaching with her quarterstaff, and before she can react, Elowen bashes Vesper hard in the chest. Just moments later, the glass dagger plunges into Vesper’s back. Breathless, bleeding, and half-blind, she falls unconscious.
Aelyra casts Faerie Fire in the room in the hopes that it highlights the invisible imp, but the imp happens not to be in the range of the cube. He remains unseen. Belvedere, not yet realizing that he is engulfed in light, attempts to vanish in a plume of smoke, but the outline of his frame be seen clearly through his hazy shroud thanks to the faerie fire. Syren has drawn her crossbow, and fires a bold directly into the haze, piercing Belvedere.
Despite this pain, Elowen hears Belvedere’s voice call to her again, saying, “Now go and get my horn.” And Elowen turns towards Aelyra, who had the horn tucked away in her pack. Aelyra sees Elowen approaching, realizing what she has just done to Vesper, thinks quickly. She casts mage hand, ripping the quarterstaff from the absentminded Elowen’s graps and flinging it to Belvedere. The blow lands hard, bashing the side of his head near the stump that remains from his severed horn. He stumbles, the smoke from his attempt to disappear fades as he loses concentration on his spell. As Belvedere stumbles and falls, Syren fires a shot, but misses because of his unpredictable swaying.
The quarterstaff being torn from Elowen’s grasp and the interruption of Belvedere’s focus allows Elowen to break free of his spell. With no memory of what has transpired since the spell was cast, she looks around to take stock of the situation. Aelyra mouths to her, “I’m sorry”. Elowen realizes she’s moved to a completely different part of the room. Her spell focus–the quarterstaff–has been flung at the demon who’s lying on the floow surrounded by a cube of light. Vesper is bleeding out on the floor just behind her. Ever the healer, she rushes to Vesper’s side and casts Spare the Dying, stopping the bleeding and preventing the death of her new friend.
Aelyra has one more trick up her sleeve. She casts Dissonant Whisper, filling Belvedere’s demonic head with a terrible song of pain and torture. The demon tries to flee, but his body is weak and broken, and the pain becomes too much to bear. His hot demon blood leaks from his eyes and nose and ears, and he writhes in pain… until he doesn’t. The demon is dead.
Max, seeing his nemesis slain, calls out, “Huh! It’s time to end this! It’s over, and we are going home!”
Huh reveals himself, his fury glints in his black eyes, and he rushes towards Max, screeching “That was my master, you fool!” But Max deftly flies up over Huh and slams down on top of him. He turns to Aelyra and says to her, “Thank you for freeing us. I will take care of him, you guys can do whatever you want in here. We’ll be gone by morning.”
Elowen tends to Vesper, casting Cure Wounds to seal the wound from Huh’s glass dagger once and for all. Syren retrieves Findlay’s finger from the warding circle, breaking the ward and allowing him to return to the lamp shop. Vesper and Elowen continue their search of Findlay’s suite, each finding one of his spell books. Then, the party bids farewell to the imps, who are already preparing to return through the portal, and they head back to the Lute & Lyre.
data.breaking-into-the-lamp-emporium#Breaking:
The players follow Findlay back to the Lamp Emporium. Findlay points to a mark on the ground and says, “I can’t get any closer than that to the building.” The players test the ward, ensuring that they are not also kept out by the magic. They are not, and so Vesper approaches the primary entrance which has a poorly written and heavily mispelled sign that says, “Closed. Reopening under new management. -B”. She tries the door, but finds it locked, and so she produces her thieves kit and picks the lock, which is a little more complex than she’s accustomed to, but she gets it unlocked without getting anyone’s attention and takes a peek inside to scope out the situation.
Peering through the door, Vesper can see three imps on the floor of a well-stocked lamp emporium show room. Two of them–one, a skunk-like imp with two parallel stripes running along its back, and the other a small gray demon with enormous pointed ears and a thin tail with a sharp barb at the end of it–are painting a new sign for the lamp emporium. The third, a slightly bigger but still relatively small green creature, paced back and forth with a club, overseeing the sign, nodding with approval at the mispelled words and malformed letters.
Vesper returns to the party to tell them what she saw, and she suggests a silent approach. Syren expresses that she feels confident that she would walk in and kill the imps with no need for secrecy, stating that she is “really powerful”. Aelyra suggests that, perhaps they don’t kill the cute little guys, but instead, perhaps they could persuade them, and she even suggests using some of her magic to do it. Vesper seems to like that plan, suggesting that they try to simply buy a lamp, or ask for a tour of the lamp emporium. “And then kill them?” Syren suggests, and Aelyra says, “No no no… I think that these imps deserve to live.” They start to think about Findlay and his motives, starting to doubt whether they can trust someone who enslaved these creatures, and consider helping the imps instead.
After a discussion about what to do with the imps and Findlay, the party decides to side with the imps and to secure their freedom fully, finding the enslavement of the small infernal creatures to be morally abhorrent, despite their impish nature. The plot consists of simply entering the Lamp Emporium and offering to help Belvedere secure the Lamp Emporium and to help keep Findlay at bay, for a price. Syren offers several times to kill Findlay, to the objections of the rest of the group. Aelyra wants to ease into the situation with a little bit of magical assistance, so she plans to discretely cast Charm Person on the bigger green imp prior to entering the room.
And so they do that. Aelyra very quietly opens the door, reaches her hand inside, and casts Charm person towards the green imp. The spell binds successfully, but the imps all notice the spell being cast from across the room. The larger imp takes no action, being under Aelyra’s spell, but the other two imps take action immediately. They drop their paintbrushes and one of the imps–a small, grey one–opens his mouth and breathes out enormous plumes of smoke, filling the room. Aelyrca shouts through the smoke and fog at the imp under her spell, telling him they just want to talk, and he calms his fellow imps down and asks what she wants. Aelyra explains the proposition to the imp, named Biff, who quietly expresses disdain towards Belvedere and says, “You want to help us? I got someone else you should talk to, come with me.” Aelyra calls the rest of her party in and they follow the imp up the stairs.
The second floor is a workshop, with many various lamps in progress, a kiln, and some imps making lamp s there. A small bat-like imp is also working, and that is who Biff takes them to. He says, “Max, these people want to talk to Belvedere”, to which Max replies, “Oh… Fuck Belvedere. What do you want with him?” Max reveals that Belvedere is powerful, and wants to crush all of Norville, but the Imps just want to return to their native plane and want no part in Belvedere’s overarching evil plan, but when Findlay nulled their contracts, Belvedere immediately bound the impish contracts under his control. The players are reluctant, and ask for a reward to help them, to which Max says that they have no money, but they can have whatever is in the lamp emporium that they want. Vesper asks for their tails in exchange instead, and Max immediately agrees to cut his tail off and says that it’s a small price to pay, though he also tells the players that not all of the imps are on board with overthrowing Belvedere.
While this discussion is happening, Syren and Vesper look around to see which imps in the room are in agreement and realize that one of the imps–a small, adorable pink imp named Yuck–is trying to sneak up the stairs to the next floor away from them, and they both sprint after him to bring him back. Syren trips and falls, still feeling the liquor in her belly. Vesper leaps over the prone Syren and grabs the imp by the scruff of the neck, pulling it back into the room with the rest of them. The pink imp begins yelling about how Belvedere will not let Max or the elves get away with their plot against him, and that he’s powerful.
Syren, still on the floor, says, “I have a lot of power.”
Vesper begins interrogating the pink imp, wanting to know Belvedere’s weaknesses and how to find and defeat him, but Yuck is defiant and spits acid at her. Vesper, frustrated with the stubbornness, cuts off the imp’s tail and wraps it around her neck like a scarf. After a lot of fruitless (but very spit-ful) back and forth between Yuck and Vesper, Syren steps in and begins taking fingers. Yuck caves and tells the players that Belvedere loves impish bon-bons. After getting the information from Yuck, Syren slits Yuck’s throat, killing him.
data.finding-belvedere#Finding Belvedere:
Max, having listened in to the elve’s interrogation, leans in and tells tells Vesper that he knows that there are impish Bonbons on the showroom counter. She runs downstairs to grab them, taking a couple of gold coins from the cash register and replacing them with her chocolates.
After that, Max tells the party that Belvedere stays in Findlay’s quarters, and he leads them up the stairs to the fourth floor. As they pass through the third, more adorable little imps watch on. Since the players are being accompanied by Max, they look away as if to say, “I didn’t see anything.” The players continue climbing the stairs up to the fourth floor–Findlay’s master suite.
In the suite, they see an open portal to the abyssal realm, the swirling vortex of hell just beyond. Lying on the floor in front of the portal is a welcome mat that reads “Not Welcome” and faces towards the portal, which keeps the demons and imps from being able to enter the mortal plane. In the middle of the room drawn on the floor lies a cleanly-drawn and slightly glowing incantation circle, the center of which is adorned with Findlay’s severed finger, pulsing with the magic of the ward that keeps the rest of his physical body out.
There is no sign of anyone in the room.
The party derives plans to search the room. Vesper begins searching through bookshelves, desks, etc. Looking for some sort of information about what sort of work is happening here, and also hoping to find Findlay’s spellbook. She doesn’t uncover anything of note. Syren skips back down to the third floor to see if she can find Belvedere there and get the drop on him. She sees some cute little imps, but no sign of Belvedere there. Aelyra is looking for signs of recent occupancy, checking for warm candles, ruffles bed dressings, fresh smells in the chamberpot, anything like that. Elowen is keeping watch for the demon more generally, looking for signs of him possibly hiding magically, and opening windows in the hopes that the wind reveals something to her.
Aelyra finds a big massive dump in the commode, still warm with the heat of the bowels from which they exited (sorry Alex, that’s probably pretty gross), so someone was certainly here recently. As she is about to walk away from the chamber pot, she gives it a final tap, which triggers a hidden mechanism and opens a hidden compartment in the bottom, and inside of it is a broken demon’s horn. She gathers the party together to share and discuss her findings. As they muse about the horn, its former owner, and the implications of its detached state, the wind blows from an open window and across the room, encircling the portal. As Elowen turns to see what the wind is trying to tell her, the others follow her gaze towards the portal from which a demon emerges and asks in a gentle voice, “uh, can I uhh, have that back please?” He gestures towards the horn. The demon is Belvedere, who is of average height and size, looking more human than demon, with one of his horns broken off.
“You can’t have that back,” says Syren.
“I dont think you can prove this is yours,” says Vesper.
“Huh!”, says Belvedere.
The party froze, somewhat confused.
“Not you. Huh!” And following the second call of the word “Huh,” a small white imp with black eyes comes through the portal as well. The party notice now that the demon and imp are both wearing special passes around their necks that allow them to pass through the portal. The imp is named Huh, and as soon as he comes into the room, the room fills with the acrid smell of ammonia and chemicals. The glint of a lamp light just barely reflects off of his sharp glass knife and catches Elowen’s eye, before Huh becomes invisible entirely.
“Yeah, I’m gonna need that back,” Belvedere says.
Syren gives Vesper some of her bardic inspiration before Vesper offers him some impish bonbons as a means to make a deal with Belvedere and call off Huh, possibly just to buy themselves some time. “We’re just trying to talk,” she says. Max watches on silently.
Belvedere says, “I would like my horn first, thank you very much”.
“We were offered money for this horn, you should give us money for it.”
“Hmm… how about I promise you won’t get stabbed by my friend who’s floating around here if you give me my horn back.”
Vesper pulls an Impish Bonbon from her bag and shows it to Belvedere.
“Hmm… have you ever had one of those?”
“They’re pretty spicy.”
“Go ahead, have one! That looks like a really good one.” He pulls an impish bonbon from his own pocket and says, “cheers?”
They both take a bite of their impish bonbons. Immediately, Vesper notes how it tastes like raw flour, but Vesper chews on defiantly. Then her stomach turns and she begins to feel nauseous, like she is about to vomit, but the vomit never comes. All of a sudden, her body goes weightless, her vision goes black for a moment, her senses are gone, and when it comes back, the colors are all inverted and wrong, and she can’t really remember who anyone is or what she is doing there. She begins consulting with Marzipan, the only thing she recognizes.
Belvedere says, “I guess you can’t hang. Do you mind if I take this?” And Vesper just hands over the box of impish bonbons, confused.
Then he turns to Syren. “So, how about that horn?”
data.findlay#Findlay:
The party returns to find Findlay fast asleep at a table. The tavern is quiet, everyone has filtered out. It is late in the night. The party wakes him and tells them what happened, for the most part. Findlay offers to pay for the imp tail around Vesper’s neck, but she declines, saying she’d rather keep it. He inquires about the horn, and they say they couldn’t find it, nor could they find his spellbooks, suggesting that they could be beyond the abyssal portal in his office.
Findlay wonders how he will get more imp servants, and Aelyra suggests that he instead hire actual workers in the future and pay them, rather than relying on slave labor. He seems to consider the option before bidding the party good night and heading back to his home. The players retire to their quarters in the tavern to rest and recover, waiting to see what the next day holds for them.
data.highlights#Highlights: The characters all meet in the Norville tavern, The Lute & Lyre, and prepare for a performance. During Vesper and Aelyra’s performance, a man bursts through the door pleading for help He is the owner of the Lamp Emporium, and tells everyone that he spilled tea on his demonic contracts that bound a demon and several imps to his servitude, which voided the contracts and freed the demon and imps. He’s lost controls of his shop and needs help breaking the ward, killing the infernal creatures, and getting back into his shop and home. The characters agree to help! They head to the lamp emporium and Vesper picks the lock of the main entrance They find some imps on the showroom floor painting a sign, planning to open the shop the following day Having a change of heart and considering the nature of the enslavement, the players decide to instead help Belvedere retain control of the lamp emporium for a price. Aelyra casts Charm person on one of the imps (Biff), who takes them to their de facto leader Max, who is planning a rebellion against the Demon Belvedere, who has reinstated the contracts for himself. After a discussion with Max regarding Belvedere’s desires to destroy Norville, the party has another change of heart and decides to kill Belvedere for the imps, freeing them of their binding contracts. The party discovers an imp sneaking away, likely to inform Belvedere. They catch him, torture him, discover Belvedere’s weakness, and then kill him and take his tail. The party then searched Belvedere’s quarters for any signs of life, for the spellbook–anything. Aelyra finds the demon Belvedere’s horn. Belvedere and his closest ally imp Huh emerge from an abyssal portal in the quarters and demand the horn back. Vesper eats an Impish Bonbon, trying to gain Belvedere’s trust to buy some time, and is immediately set into a crippling confusion. Elowen is hypnotized by Belvedere, causing her to attack Vesper. Vesper is stabbed by Huh, who has turned invisible, and stabs her into unconsciousness. Aelyra casts an illuminating spell, preventing Belvedere from disappearing. Syren shoots him with a crossbow bolt. Elowen comes to attack Aelyra, but thinking quickly, she uses her Mage Hand to tear the quarterstaff from her grip and to fling it at Belvedere, injuring him severely. She then casts Dissonaant Whisper, which overwhelms the weakened Belvedere and kills him. Elowen snaps out of it and saves the dying Vesper, bringing her back to good health. The imps are freed, and the party has salvaged rewards in their own way, both from Findlay and from retrieving objects.

data.the-lute--lyre#The Lute \u0026amp; Lyre:
The story starts in the mid-sized trade town of Norville. It’s a wet, cold, stinky, rainy spring day, some time between 2 and 4 pm, maybe 3 pm, who’s to say, live your own truth or whatever. Four adventurers are coincidentally drawn to Norville for one reason or another.
Elowen Giggleleaf, the mysterious druid (NOT cleric, thank you very much) was drawn to Norville by the wind, which told her that a beautiful white horse had an injury and needed her help. She found the horse behind the local tavern called The Lute & Lyre, lying in a stable, injured. Drawing upon her earthly magic, she healed the horse, who gave her a nod and a wink as if to say, “thanks bro, good lookin’ out”.
Vesper Dreadway arrived at 3:00 pm as is her own truth and entered the Lute & Lyre. She’s been here before, and she’ll be back again. She begins to set up to perform, but has arrived a bit early. The tavern is dead, save for a few poor souls already drunk. The coffers are clearly running dry among the patrons here. Even still, the day is early, and she hopes that later on, more people start filing in.
Aelyra Caladwen and Syren Ashryver arrive shortly after Vesper, with the specific intent of Aelyra performing. Aelyra immediately takes note of the stage AND the person on it and immediately thinks, “Oh, her and I could play together, cool!” Aelyra approaches Vesper, who is preparing the space for her performance, and says, “Hey, I see you got an instrument. Yeah. I also have an instrument. Where are you gonna play that instrument? I was gonna do a little ditty.” She gestures towareds Syren. “This is my friend. She doesn’t have instruments, but she’s cool. She’s here… She’s here for the vibes, okay? And I need money, too.”
Syren injerjects on Aelyra’s behalf while Aelyra tunes her lyre (a.k.a. baby harp). She invoked Aelyra’s status as high nobility of a neighboring country, but Vesper is unimpressed by the credentials. Aelyra begins playing a beautiful quiet ballad-type of song, invoking tears in the eyes of the drunk men all around. Vesper watches, largely unimpressed though silently acknowledging some amount of talent there, straps on her Lute and begins playing Bon Jovi’s “Livin’ on a Prayer”, which also invokes tears. Vesper agrees to allow Aelyra to play as backup, but must follow Vesper’s lead. Aelyra agrees, reluctantly.
The characters spend the next few hours “getting hammer drunk” and waiting for more patrons to file in before performing. Hours later, when the tavern finally appears to be sufficiently populated, the musicians take the stage and begin playing what may or may not have been Bob Marley’s “Jammin’”, and the patrons love it. They’re eating it up.
Mere moments into the performance, a man bursts through the tavern door in a panic, shouting for help in a panic. Vesper vaguely recognizes the man as the owner of the Lamp Emporium, and she and Aelyra stop playing to listen to what he has to say. He notices that he has the attention of the people nearby and continues, rubbing his cheeks with his palms nervously:
I’ve spilled tea all over my demonic contracts at the at the lamp shop and now the demon and all the imps that I had serving me are freed and I don’t know what to do. They rebelled and kicked me out of the lamp emporium. I can’t get back in. They’re running the place, Oh, I need to get back in there, I have important blueprints and my spellbook, they have everything. Belvedere, my demon servant, took my finger and is using it to bind a ward that keeps me from being able to enter! Are any of you adventureres that can help me? I can offer many rewards!
Aelyra immediately agrees to help, and as a result of that, Syren also agrees to help, but only to help Aelyra and keep her out of trouble. Elowen, who has been silently observing from the corner, emerges and also agrees to assist, insisting that she wants to ensure that nobody gets hurt. Vesper expresses some reluctance, and asks, “Well, what’s in it for me?”
Findlay lays out his terms. The Imps must be dealt with, and for every imp tail brought to him, he will pay four gold. For one of Belvedere’s horns, he will also pay, and he will also pay if Belvedere is demonstrably killed or banished from the natural plane. He will pay for the return of his finger, for the breaking of the ward, for the discovery and return of his spellbook, and for a blueprint for a special lamp that he is working on. Elowen asks, “Can I have a lamp?” to which Findlay agrees unconditionally. Vesper decides to join, but asks Findlay to watch her lute, to which he also agrees.

data.highlights#Highlights: The party wakes up in Norville the morning after the Lamp Emporium incident, feeling stronger and wiser. Elowen communes with the wind and receives a vision: enslaved imps in chains, laboring under the sun near the elven castle of Squawhorn, and dozens of demonic contracts with the signature Gwarveaux. Aelyra comes downstairs to find a letter waiting for her, sealed with the crest of the Twilight Court. Her father knows she’s gone. The party, motivated by the vision and by Aelyra’s need to put some distance between herself and whoever her father sends after her, agrees to head to Squawhorn and free the enslaved imps. On the road, Vesper finds a buyer for part of Yuck’s tail, trading it in exchange for having her dagger and a new amulet imbued with the imp’s acidic essence. The party stumbles across a wizard’s tower that definitely wasn’t there when they passed this way before. With a storm rolling in, they decide to spend the night inside. The tower is a time loop. The party dies a lot. It’s fine. On their way through the tower, they encounter giant rats, mud mephits with sticky fingers, a talking riddle door, a magical mirror that does unsettling things, and a Nothic who has been trapped in the tower so long that it has warped and twisted him into something unrecognizable. The party fights the Nothic and wins, then destroys the magical orb at the top of the tower, freeing a skeleton who’s been trapped inside cleaning the same room for who knows how long, and escaping into the sunlight.
data.morning-in-norville#Morning in Norville:
The morning after the Lamp Emporium, the sun is rising and the Lute & Lyre is quiet. The smell of beer and breakfast rise up through the floor boards and into the inn chambers. Birds sing and chirp outside, deaf to the hellish events of the night before.
Elowen is the first to stir. She opens the window of her little room and lets the wind in, closing her eyes as it washes over her. But this morning the wind has something to say. The air grows hot and strange — hotter than any spring morning has any business being — and it encircles her, faster and faster, like a growing whirlwind.
In the window of her mind, she can see the wind carrying with it dozens and dozens of pages, swirling around her. She reaches out in her mind and snatches one from the air. The page is covered in text, written in some foul demonic language that she cannot comprehend. It appears to be a contract. At the bottom of the page, in the common tongue, is a single signature which reads the name Gwarveaux.
Looking up, past the swirling of pages, she looks to the sun setting on the horizon. Hundreds or thousands of imps in chains, tilling fields and hauling carts, the silhouette of the elven castle of Squawhorn looming behind them.
As the wind calms and cools, the image fades from her mind but the memory remains. She opens her eyes and goes down to the dining hall.
Aelyra comes downstairs for breakfast and is informed by the morning bartender that a letter arrived for her. After the bartender spends an embarrassing amount of time failing to locate said letter, Aelyra finds it herself. It was sitting in plain sight, sealed with the unmistakable crest of the Twilight Court. The letter is brief, and reads:
Dearest Alira,
We know that you have exited our land, and we are coming for you.
From,
Your Lord Father
P.S. Don’t trust everyone you meet.
Aelyra sighs, folds the envelope and puts it away. Out in the tavern she spots Elowen sitting at the same table that she silently observed from the night prior, before the events at the lamp emporium. She takes a seat next to Elowen.
Vesper wakes up thinking, inexplicably, about Syren. There’s something about her — something Vesper can’t quite name, a familiarity that she can’t account for. She lies in bed turning it over for a moment before Marzipan quacks her back to reality, and she gets up and heads downstairs to join the others.
Syren comes downstairs last, looking especially in rough shape. Sunglasses hide her bloodshot eyes, a half-empty water bottle barely held in her loose grasp. She stops by the front desk, requests a couple of aspirin, and throws them back as she slowly walks towards the table with the rest of the party.
The four of them end up at a table together. “I hope they have pancakes,” says Aelyra.
They do.
As the party eats, Aelyra shares the letter and discusses the contents. Elowen recognizes the seal of the Twilight Court, which reminds her of the vision, and so she shares the details of that. Imps in chains at Squawhorn, where Aelyra’s father resides,
“What’s in it for me?” asks Vesper. Classic rogue.
Aelyra lists all of the treasures available in the Twilight Court, including magical lamps and daggers. She promises Vesper a ruby-encrusted magical dagger named Delilah from her father’s treasury, and Elowen expresses interest in a magical lamp.
The group agrees: they’re going to Squawhorn.
data.okay-this-is-getting-ridiculous#Okay, Th:
Elowen sighs. “Okay, burn the wizard’s tower down.” The players turn towards the door that they just came from–it’s the front door, the main entrance that they initially took to get in. They consider just leaving the tower, here and now, and abandoning this place. But they decide against it. They decide to press on ahead.
Elowen approaches the door and knocks three time, again to no response. They open the door. More fucking stairs.
As they enter the second floor, once again the door behind them locks, only this time the ceiling begins to lower on them. Panicked, they all race towards the door. Vesper dashes expertly towards the end, but the others just don’t have the drive to do it. As the ceiling lowers and they have less room to run, they’re pushed down into the floor. The ceiling presses on them, squeezes them. Everything goes black.
They come to back where they just were, at the first floor, with the three torches lit before them. They all touch their bodies, vividly remembering their deaths from just seconds ago. “What the hell?”
They compose themselves, and Aelyra gets an idea to construct some sort of “situation” with the debris that litters the first floor to keep the ceiling from coming down. Again, they climb up the stairs and rush into the room. Aelyra quickly places her situation and dashes towards the door. This time, it’s Vesper who doesn’t quite make it in time, and is crushed by the ceiling.
Back to the entrance.
Okay, one last attempt: Aelyra and the party really put their best foot forward in constructing the situation. It’s well built. Again, they go up the stairs. Again, they rush in and emplace the situation, and this time, the party makes it through all together, and they ascend once more into the room with the mirror room.
Now, as they enter, written in large letters across the entire mirror is the name Aelyra, in dripping warm blood. Vesper places a single hand on the mirror and asks, “Mirror mirror on the wall, who’s the fairest of them all?” and her reflection smiles and winks at her. She then draws her dagger, enchanted with magic from the imp’s tail, and stabs her own reflection.
As soon as the dagger makes contact with the mirror, a pink hue spreads across the mirror, freezing the reflections in place. This gives Aelyra an idea, and she draws from her pack Belvedere’s horn and stabs it in the same place where Vesper’s dagger stabbed. From there, the mirror turns black, which also spreads out from that point. As the darkness spreads across the plane, disembodied whispering voices fill the room.
Aelyra casts Vicious Mockery, absolutely roasting the disembodied voices around them. She says, “You fucking suck man. I don’t want to do this anymore, the stairs suck as hard as you do.”
A whisper from the cacophony responds, “We are trapped here too.”
The party gasps. Aelyra questions whether or not absolutely roasting the shit out of other victims of this tower was a good idea when again, a singular voice pierces through the noise with a warning.
“They replaced us. Don’t let them replace you.”
The party stands silently for a little bit before moving on to the next floor, absorbing the warning they just receive.
Once they arrive on the fourth floor, the room is scorched. Soot and burn marks everywhere. Three Magmin are sitting quietly in a corner. When they notice the party enter, they immediately spring into action. “We want something to burn! We want something to burn! Give us something to burn! Give us something to burn!”
Aelyra says, “Can you burn the mirror because that shit’s annoying.”
“Fuck that thing!”
Vesper says, “Yes. Go freaking melt it with your magma hand.”
“It doesn’t work! It won’t burn!”
Elowen says, “Burn the house down.”
“I need to burn something!”
Vesper offers the torch she’s holding, realizing that it’s not necessary. THe Magmin takes it in his hands and it immediately burns to ash. “That’s not enough! I need more! Something to burn!”
All of the players hand over their torches. They have dark vision. Why did they even have these torches, like honestly? Kind of funny. But the torches don’t sate the little Magmin, who are once again bouncing off the walls. “Please! More to burn!”
Vesper says, “Okay, we’ll get you something. Wait for us, we’ll be back.” And the players back track all the way down to the first floor, where they planned to get some wood. But as they make their way down, Vesper realizes how frustrated she is with all of this, and when they get there, she immediately heads for the front door. “Fuck this, I’m done,” she says, and she tries to open this front door, but finds it won’t give way.
“Of course it’s locked,” she says, dejected.
Aelyra and Elowen, at the same time, both say, “What if they burn the door?”
Aelyra says, “Yes, bring them down and burn this door.”
“No,” Elowen says. “Send them up to burn the face door. I’m done with his riddles. I’m done with being teleported. Either I’m going to anamorph if I have to, or he’s going to get burned.”
While the two discuss what they want to do, Vesper gives it some thought. She thinks of all the creatures they’ve seen so far. The family of giant Rats. The Mephits, who seemed harmless overall. The trapped souls whispering from within the glass mirror. The front door feels too easy, there must be some reward at the end of all this.
“Let’s burn the face-ass bitch,” says Vesper.
The party returns to the Magmin with some wood, which again burns too quickly. The players tell the Magmin about the door upstairs, to which one says, “Door? Why didn’t I think of door?” And they burn their way up the stairs into the next room.
The face door greets the players heartily. “Ha ha! Welcome back! I see you are ready for another–what are you doing? Oh! Oh! Oh! Noooo!” And the face door burns, gone completely. Tired and satisfied, the Magmin sit back down to rest, and fall asleep.
The players climb the stairs once more.

Gold
200 Gold Pieces found in a chest at the top of the tower, divided as the players see fit Note: the mud mephits on Floor 4 quietly pickpocketed all previously held gold from the party during negotiations Aelyra
1 Torn Bag of Holding that needs to be repaired Elowen
1 Wizard’s Spell Book Spell Scrolls Vesper
Acid Dagger (one dagger imbued with Yuck’s tail — deals extra acid damage) Amulet of Acid/Poison Resistance (amulet imbued with Yuck’s tail. once per day, advantage on saving throws against poison or acid) 1 Bomb (found in the tower) Wizardly candelabras and assorted shiny objects
data.the-market#The Market:
Before leaving Norville, the party swings by the market for supplies — rations, bedrolls, the basics for a few days of road travel. It’s while browsing that the imp named Yuck’s tail, draped around Vesper’s neck, catches the eye of a strange masked merchant at a nondescript and seemingly empty stand.
“Excuse me, young miss, but where’d you get that?” he asks.
The merchant turns out to know his infernal materials. He identifies the tail by its color and smell as belonging to an imp of an acidic, poisonous nature, and offers to work it into something useful. He knows Ratwhistle. He knows Vesper’s father, Thad, and they bond over Thad Miller.
She walks away with one of her daggers imbued with the tail’s acidic properties — it now deals extra acid damage on a hit and has taken on a distinctly pinkish hue — and a matching amulet that provides resistance against poison and acid once per day. The merchant keeps what’s left of the tail. Everyone is happy.
The party loads up and heads out of Norville, bound eastward for Squawhorn.
data.what-the-fuck-is-going-on#What the Fuck:
“No way,” Vesper says.
The door they just came through seems to have circled right back to the beginning. But, how is that possible? Aelyra tries to take the torches off the wall, but they’re firmly affixed. She knocks on the door twice. But there is no answer, only the silence of time passing by.
“Well,” says Aelyra. And they go back up, clearly growing frustrated with this place.
As they enter the familiar second floor, the door behind them closes, and the room begins to fill with a noxious gas. Very quickly, their vision is obscured and maintaining a sense of direction becomes difficult as the gas disorients them mentally. Aelyra, Syren, and Elowen all make it to the door in time, but Vesper becomes lost in the fog. As her vision dims, she calls out for help. Elowen hears her calls, takes in a deep breath, and sprints back into the room in the direction of the calls. She finds Vesper and sprints back towards the exit. Everyone is safe, and up the stairs they go.
The third floor once again has the long mirror, but opposite the mirror are several portraits that were not there before. Each portrait is a near identical portrait of Vesper, but as they go further and further into the room, each portrait has a smile that grows larger and larger and larger, until at the end the smile is almost too large for her face.
Vesper draws one of her daggers and slashes the first portrait, to no apparent effect except to reveal the brick wall behind the canvas. She approaches the next one and starts slapping it and tries to remove it from the wall. But nothing happens. They turn towards the mirror, looking for any sign of something happening, but nothing. They all look pretty good in this mirror, actually. Nice.
Vesper becomes enraged. They only came into this stupid tower to rest through a storm, and now they’re being tormented. One by one, Vesper violently slashes all of the paintings, and at the end, when they are all slashed and nothing has happened, they sigh and move on up the stairs.
As they enter the fourth floor, it is this time completely covered with mud, Piles of it all over the room, the walls and ceiling are essentially coated with it. Strange, they think, and as they wade through, Mud Mephits arise from the mud. The foremost mephit gestures towards Aelyra with its hands outstretch and palms open. Aelyra recognizes the gesture and lies, “Oh but I only have six gold pieces!”
The party gathers to discuss the amount of gold that they have. Aelyra turns back and says, “How much gold do you want, little guy?”
“I wants the moneys and treasures!” it responds.
“Oh, well how much money and treasures do you want?”
“As much as you has!”
“Well, I have six whole pieces for you right here. Do you want six of them?”
"…I thinks you has more…"
“I have a fake mustache. You want that?”
The Mephits begin to rabble a little bit, speaking over one another, negotiating the demands.
From behind Aelyra, a Mephit sniffs around her pack and announces, “I smells a demon on this one.”
Aelyra calls out, “Let me see the key, please!” The Mephits all stop talking. One of them in the back, a smaller one, holds up the key which is almost too big for his hands and calls out, “I has the key!” Everyone is enamored with that little guy. What a freaking cutie.
Aelyra calls out, “Okay well I have six gold pieces and this little horn,” and she produces from her pack Belvedere’s horn.
A mephit turns to Elowen. “What about you?” She replies, “I also have six gold pieces, and I will give them to you. Also I have a lamp.”
“No! I think I need more treasure.”
“But it’s a really nice lamp. It’s magical. Imps made it.”
“Let me see inside your pack.”
“See inside my pack? I can’t do that. There’s tampon in there, I have feminine products. You perv!”
The mephits turn to Vesper and give her the same interrogation.
“I have seven gold pieces!” And she produces six gold pieces and one of her chocolate coins. “This one is a human delicacy, it’s great. Try it!”
The mephit takes the coin and bites right into it, through the foil and all. Everyone winces as they think about biting into that thing with a filling or something, ugh, that sucks to even think about. Even one of the other mephits cringes a little bit.
“That’s okay… the Mephit says.
“I have more of those! I have a lot more!”
Syren, through her sunglasses, takes a sip of the coffee and rubs her throbbing head. She watches through her hangover the mephits confer with one another, discussing. Several mephits sink into the mud, and the foremost mephit remains. “That is a deal, we will takes your golds and your chocolates and your lamps. We don’t wants no demon horns though, too dangerous.”
The small mephit arises from the mud and hands the key to Syren while everyone else hands over the meager amounts of gold and trinkets that they offered, completely unaware of the mephits rooting around in their packs behind them, stealing all of the gold from within.
The lead mephit laughs, thanks the party kindly, and sinks into the mud with the others.
The players travel up to the next floor. The door greets them again, remembering them, and poses another riddle: “I have a neck but no head, and I wear a cap but have no hair. What am I?” Aelyra knows this one. “A bottle!” The door opens, and they climb the stairs…
…to find themselves back at the entrance again. Now, a third torch is lit above the door.
data.where-did-that-tower-come-from#Where Did:
The road to Squawhorn runs roughly four days on foot. The party makes good time on the first day, moving through open country and farmland. Sometime in the late afternoon of the second day, with a storm building dark and fast on the horizon, they come around a bend in the road and see a tower in the distance.
Tall, narrow, slightly crooked, with moss growing up one side and vines beginning to reclaim the lower stones. The towering tower towers over them, toweringly. It looks completely abandoned. Neither Syren nor Aelyra recall seeing this tower on this road when they just passed through mere days prior. It is strange.
Elowen pays close attention to the storm, looking for signs as to whether or how they can weather it. She concludes that camping in it could be very dangerous. The tower is right there. It’s not doing anything. It’s just standing there being a tower, almost inviting them in, offering the comfort and safety that they need.
They go inside.
The inside of the tower is exactly what the outside promised: dusty, dim, cobwebbed, full of broken crates that have been empty long enough to start rotting. There is a single door across the room, and above it, one torch burning on the wall. No footprints in the dust. The only entrance is the door they came in through.
Vesper presses her ear to the door and hears nothing. She opens it and finds a climbing stairwell. They go up.
The second floor is more of the same — dark, quiet, abandoned, the kind of place that suggests no one has been here in a very long time but something still feels subtly wrong about the texture of the dust and the wear on the walls. The party investigates rigorously, meticulously. They all come to the same conclusion: the age of this place doesn’t feel natural. Like something is maintaining the aesthetic of abandonment without fully committing to it.
Without anything actionable, and instead just the vague notion of inauthenticity, they keep moving towards the door across the room, and up another stairwell.
This floor is different: instead of a large, circular room, it’s more of a long hallway. One wall, floor to ceiling, is entirely occupied by a single enormous mirror, and another unassuming door lies in the wall at the far end. Similarly to the room below, something about this mirror gives them a vague sense of dread. They inspect the mirror, but nothing seems obvious.
As they pass, Aelyra looks in the mirror. For a brief moment, it appears that her reflection blinks when she does not. She stares. It doesn’t do it again, but something is definitely wrong with this mirror.
Again, they go through the door and up another stairwell.
The fourth floor is not unoccupied. A family of giant rats who have set up a nest in a corner of the room and are deeply uninterested in sharing the space. The characters walk past the rats and straight towards the next door, but this time find it locked. After a lot of searching, the key to the locked door is found… lying in the rat’s nest.
Elowen attempts to befriend them with her animal friendship spell. The rats, however, are not interested in friendship. They’re interested in maintaining their personal space. COVID rules and all that, please.
The party retreats to the staircase to regroup and brainstorm some ideas. Aelyra decides that she will just retrieve the key with her Mage Hand spell. The Mage Hand reaches into the nest, takes the key, and retreats with the rats none the wiser. The lock opens. They go through, and up more stairs.
The door to the fifth floor has a large serene-looking face, eyes and mouth closed, carved into the wood. As the party approaches, the eyes open and the mouth says, in the bored tone of someone who has been doing this for a very long time:
“Are you looking to enter?”
They are.
“I will only let you in if you answer my riddle.”
He presents his riddle: What must be broken before it can be used?
Vesper knows this one. “An egg!”
“Correct!” The face opens the door. They go through. They go up the stairs. They come out on the first floor, back where they came in. Across the room, a second torch is now lit on the wall, beside the first.
